newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses direction, chased by NY rise.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses direction, chased by NY rise.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures, reversing its earlier weaker direction, flipped up by the close on industry and trade price-fixing, helped by soaring New York values, traders said.
But activity remained lethargic and the day's volume of 4,177 lots comprised mainly AA trades against May as well as May/July switches.
Roasters and traders jumped in to fix prices of their earlier contracts as the market took an upward path.
Many also rolled forward their May positions ahead of the contract's first notice day.
But market watchers doubt there would be fresh business as many roasters were still taking stock of inventory levels.
Sellers, however, were still wary since the Brazilian frost season is just around the corner.
Benchmark May rebounded from a low of $1,550 a tonne to end the day $15 higher at $1,585.
It had hit an intraday peak was $1,590 but failed to clear stiff resistance at a chart gap between $1,590 and $1,610.
The May/July spread narrowed to level money by the close, against $6 premium on Tuesday.
New York arabica futures marched higher aided by technical buying as the market triggered buy-stops at 183 cents a lb on May.
By 1627 GMT, May was seven cents up at 185.75 cents.

Traders said London's fortunes continued to hinge on New York. A break on the upside of the immediate 160-170 cent-range on July could provide the U.S. market a fresh impetus for an assault at 174 and then 177 cents.
In the physical sector, traders said the markets stayed quiet this week as European demand slowed for the higher-priced May coffee while enquiries for second half 1997 arabicas met with few sellers.
Traders said stabilising futures prices since Monday after weeks of volatility gave the market a long overdue breather but fresh deals were still hard to come by.
They noted a reasonable interest in prompt robustas to fill in cover for the Western hemisphere summer months.
In arabicas, there were enquiries for Brazilian material up to September shipments but business was slow as producers returned from the long Easter holidays.
